subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Launch and diagnostic: rhythm and meter
task_label: Music theory and listening — Diagnostic probe
essential_question: How can understanding music creation and performance help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about rhythm and meter, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of rhythm and meter.
Check, revise, or improve work about rhythm and meter using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about rhythm and meter.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: Day 1 of "Music Creation and Performance" (unit 3, grade 7) is a diagnostic probe on rhythm and meter. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Compose, arrange, or perform a short piece with a score, sequence, or listening guide. Today's work contributes to that by handling rhythm and meter at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of rhythm and meter, melody and harmony concepts, form, and notation or sequencing. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any instruction on rhythm and meter, make a short baseline response so you can see your own starting point later. Spend a few minutes producing something — a quick sketch, a short pattern, a few bars, a rough plan, or a written description if you prefer not to produce a piece today. Then write three things you already notice about rhythm and meter and one question you cannot yet answer. Keep this baseline; you will compare later work against it. Nothing here is judged for quality, only for being honest and complete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about rhythm and meter, and it belongs to "Music Creation and Performance", which also covers separate topics such as melody and harmony concepts. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rhythm and meter; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about rhythm and meter., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Activate prior knowledge about rhythm and meter, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Produce the deliverable for a diagnostic probe: Dated baseline response (made or described in writing), three noticings, and one open question, preserved for later comparison.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Dated baseline response (made or described in writing), three noticings, and one open question, preserved for later comparison.
critique_criteria: A dated baseline response to rhythm and meter exists and was made before any instruction.
Three specific noticings and one open question are recorded in writing.
The baseline is preserved for later comparison rather than discarded or overwritten.
A written description was accepted in place of a made piece if the student preferred; nothing required a camera, recording, or audience.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (rhythm and meter). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting rhythm and meter.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for rhythm and meter follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for rhythm and meter, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for rhythm and meter works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of rhythm and meter, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking rhythm and meter mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply rhythm and meter under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on rhythm and meter rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
